findings: The identical frozen RAW spatial representation supports much better training fit with the small direct50-step head than with the declared pi adapter scope under256 updates.
Frozen selected train joint RMS:small3.1499deg versus pi18.8391deg; final256 checkpoints:small2.6343deg versus pi12.0080deg. The pi fit gap is not only a checkpoint-selection artifact.

Small joint tuning improves historical held-out MSE0.33164 to0.27960 and joint RMS20.4863 to18.8080deg; selected train fit worsens3.1499 to7.5104deg. This is not a clean representation-sufficiency result.
Pi joint256 updates improve final training fit to7.9960deg but none improves validation over phase start; selection correctly remains step0. Do not call this a trained-weight generalization gain.

Measured-state-only train-fitted ridge, alpha chosen only on validation, achieves held-out joint RMS15.8250deg and MSE0.17787, outperforming all visual variants here. Visual incremental generalization has not been established.
All four selected variants fail the previously used strict training-window action fit criteria; no closed-loop success is claimed.
interpretation: Prioritize pi interface/optimization scope diagnostics while addressing visual incremental task generalization. Evidence does not uniquely blame RAW architecture, sensor noise, or insufficient total training.
limits: Historical development episodes, not an untouched benchmark
Only3 Normal training episodes and1 Normal validation episode
Different objectives/capacities; cannot infer inherent pi incapacity
Zero-visual intervention is out of distribution, not a trained state-only control
Sample seed14019; head initialization RNG restored from exact RAW850 checkpoint
No physical success or broad lighting robustness conclusion
Current RAW frame only in this simplified chain; N02 recurrent candidates/measurement corrections and auxiliaries deliberately bypassed.
5 held-out episodes are1 per light, different trajectories; not paired illumination/noise intervention.
Ridge is a lower-capacity state-only baseline, not a matched nonlinear-head ablation.
Main table uses validation-selected weights; joint phase additionally trains the head, so improvements cannot be uniquely attributed to front-end changes.

Pi joint selection is step0 with unchanged weights; held-out MSE variation0.000061 is recomputation-path variation, not parameter learning. Batch-size/kernel rounding is a hypothesis, not an isolated cause.

Use the small head as a task diagnostic, require held-out gains over state-only baselines, and independently vary image/state before attributing visual contribution.
Add a continued-frozen-head control if claiming front-end joint-training benefits; later use a new blind episode split for confirmation.
